sentences.en: I know we were just speaking about something, you know, remarkably happy and positive but this episode is tackling something that's somewhat adjacent,
sentences.zh: 我知道我们刚才还在谈论一些，你知道的，非常开心和积极的事情，但这一期我们要探讨一个可以说是有些相关

sentences.en: maybe, but also a bit different.
sentences.zh: 也许吧，但也有些不同的话题。

sentences.en: It's something a lot of us struggle with silently and that is an inability to be happy with what we have.
sentences.zh: 这是许多人都在默默挣扎的事情，那就是无法对拥有的东西感到满意。

sentences.en: That sense that something is always missing, the itch that won't go away.
sentences.zh: 那种总觉得少了点什么的感觉，那个怎么也抓耳挠腮去不掉的痒。

sentences.en: You know, you get the job and then you want a promotion.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你得到了工作，然后又想要升职。

sentences.en: You move into a new house and then suddenly you're looking for something even better or thinking about what's not right with it.
sentences.zh: 你搬进了一所新房子，然后突然间你又开始寻找更好的，或者挑剔它哪里不对劲。

sentences.en: You get into a relationship and yet there's still that lingering thought, is there something better out there for me?
sentences.zh: 你开始了一段恋爱，然而心头依然萦绕着挥之不去的想法：外面会不会有更好的人适合我？

sentences.en: Is this it?
sentences.zh: 难道就这样了吗？

sentences.en: If you are haunted by this type of thinking, you've probably found that it applies to nearly everything in your life.
sentences.zh: 如果你也饱受这种思维的折磨，你大概会发现它适用于你生活中的几乎所有事情。

sentences.en: So many of us live in this in-between space, right?
sentences.zh: 我们中有那么多人都生活在这个不上不下的中间地带，对吧？

sentences.en: This space between where we are and where we think we should be.
sentences.zh: 这个介于我们现状与我们自认为应该达到的状态之间的地带。

sentences.en: And that gap, it often feels like failure.
sentences.zh: 而这种差距，往往让人感觉像是一种失败。

sentences.en: Even if we've achieved so much, we end up living by this more, more, more mentality I've spoken about before.
sentences.zh: 即便我们已经取得了很大的成就，我们最终还是落入了那种我之前提到过的“更多、更多、更多”的心态。

sentences.en: You know, once we have what we want, all we can think about is what we don't.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，一旦我们得到了想要的，脑子里想的全都是我们没有的。

sentences.en: Meaning the bar is always being raised.
sentences.zh: 这意味着标准总是在不断提高。

sentences.en: We always want more.
sentences.zh: 我们总是想要更多。

sentences.en: We never appreciate how far we've come.
sentences.zh: 我们从不感激自己已经走过了多远。

sentences.en: So we repeatedly undervalue our progress and our happiness is the price we pay.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们一次又一次地贬低自己的进步，而我们的幸福感就是为此付出的代价。

sentences.en: I think this is also particularly compounded by the upheaval of being in our 20s where it feels like we're in competition with everyone around us.
sentences.zh: 我认为，二十岁时经历的剧烈动荡也让这一点尤为加剧，在这个时期，感觉我们好像在和周围的所有人竞争。

sentences.en: What do they have that I don't?
sentences.zh: 他们有什么是我没有的？

sentences.en: Why do they seem so much happier?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们看起来那么快乐？

sentences.en: Why does their life seem more together?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们的生活看起来更有条理？

sentences.en: How can I have that?
sentences.zh: 我怎么才能拥有那些？

sentences.en: How can I be like them?
sentences.zh: 我怎么才能像他们一样？

sentences.en: How can I feel more secure?
sentences.zh: 我怎么才能感到更有安全感？

sentences.en: The answer is we will never feel secure if we don't first understand what is driving this constant sense of dissatisfaction.
sentences.zh: 答案是，如果我们不首先弄清楚是什么在驱动这种持续的不满感，我们就永远不会感到安全。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 而且你知道吗？

sentences.en: The solution, it's more than just gratitude.
sentences.zh: 解决的办法不仅仅是感恩。

sentences.en: It's something that goes a whole lot deeper.
sentences.zh: 它要深刻得多。

sentences.en: It's probably going to surprise a few of you actually.
sentences.zh: 说实话，这可能会让你们中的一些人感到意外。

sentences.en: So my friends, I am excited to explore this psychology with you.
sentences.zh: 所以朋友们，我很兴奋能和大家一起探索这种心理学。

sentences.en: Some of you may also know I have a podcast called Mantra.
sentences.zh: 你们中的一些人可能也知道，我有一个名为《Mantra》的播客。

sentences.en: And we did a more philosophical take on this episode over there.
sentences.zh: 我们在那里对这个话题进行了更具哲学意味的探讨。

sentences.en: If you finish this and you want more,
sentences.zh: 如果你听完了这个还想要更多的话

sentences.en: Mantra is like the psychology of your 20s.
sentences.zh: 《Mantra》就像是你的二十岁心理学。

sentences.en: Soulful sister, part meditation, part inspirational.
sentences.zh: 灵魂知己，既有冥想，又具启发性。

sentences.en: Each week we give you a new mantra to focus your attention on for the week ahead.
sentences.zh: 每周我们都会给你一个新的心灵咒语，让你把注意力集中在接下来的这一周上。

sentences.en: Like some of the recent ones we've done are I release the need to do it all.
sentences.zh: 就像我们最近做过的一些主题，比如“我释放了把每件事都做到完美的需要”。

sentences.en: I trust myself to make the best decision with what I know now.
sentences.zh: “我相信自己能根据目前所知做出最好的决定。”

sentences.en: So many more.
sentences.zh: 还有很多很多。

sentences.en: It's just like the most fabulous way to start your week.
sentences.zh: 这简直是开启一周生活的绝佳方式。

sentences.en: So don't forget to check it out after that.
sentences.zh: 所以听完后别忘了去看看哦。

sentences.en: But without further ado, let's talk about why we never seem to be happy with what we have.
sentences.zh: 闲话少说，让我们来聊聊为什么我们似乎永远对拥有的东西不满意。

sentences.en: I want to explain the feeling of never being happy with what we have first here, because I really want to articulate how this feels in your body,
sentences.zh: 我想先在这里解释一下这种永远对现状不满意感觉，因为我真的很想清晰地表达出这种感觉在你的身体里

sentences.en: in your thoughts, how it looks in your day-to-day life.
sentences.zh: 在你的思绪中，以及在你的日常生活中究竟是什么样子的。

sentences.en: Because if you haven't already suspected,
sentences.zh: 因为如果你还没有过这种猜测的话

sentences.en: this feeling sounds a lot like, you know, good old-fashioned depression.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉听起来很像，你知道的，老派的抑郁症。

sentences.en: But it is different.
sentences.zh: 但它其实是不同的。

sentences.en: This contentment, happiness, treadmill as I call it, this constant pursuit of more, it's not a clinical label.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说的这种知足常乐、幸福的跑步机，这种对更多的不断追求，并不是一个临床标签。

sentences.en: Not being happy with what you have is not really something that you could be diagnosed with in the way that you could be diagnosed with a mental health disorder.
sentences.zh: 对现状不满意并不是那种你可以被诊断出来的病症，就像你被诊断出患有某种心理健康障碍那样。

sentences.en: But it may be a symptom of something larger.
sentences.zh: 但它可能是某种更大问题的症状。

sentences.en: So to be diagnosed with a major depressive disorder, you do have to meet a number of specific criteria or exhibit a number of symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，要想被诊断为重度抑郁症，你确实需要符合许多特定的标准，或者表现出许多症状。

sentences.en: A lack of satisfaction with what we have is probably going to contribute to a number of these, but it's not a symptom on its own.
sentences.zh: 缺乏对现状的满足感可能会促成其中的许多表现，但它本身并不是一个独立的症状。

sentences.en: Depression, you know, it can make even the most remarkable moments bland because of a deeper number of reactions and interactions going on below the surface.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，由于水面之下存在着更深层的反应和相互作用，抑郁症甚至能让最卓越的时刻变得索然无味。

sentences.en: So an inability to be happy with what you have may be symptomatic of that.
sentences.zh: 因此，无法对拥有的东西感到快乐，可能是那种情况的症状表现。

sentences.en: But you can also struggle with this and constantly crave more success, more accolades, more friends, more of whatever it is, whilst not being depressed,
sentences.zh: 但你也可以在没有抑郁的情况下苦于这种状态，不断渴望更多的成功、更多的荣誉、更多的朋友、更多无论什么东西，同时总体上依然感觉还算快乐，依然能够集中注意力，没有遭受失眠、疲劳这些问题的困扰。

sentences.en: while still feeling generally kind of happy, still being able to concentrate, not suffering from insomnia, fatigue, these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: （注：此处对原文语序进行了微调以确保中文通顺，但信息完全对齐）

sentences.en: The problem really occurs when this spirals and the dissatisfaction is all you seem to be able to focus on all day, every day.
sentences.zh: 真正的问题出现在这种情况陷入螺旋式上升，并且这种不满情绪似乎成了你整天、每天唯一能专注于的事情。

sentences.en: The losses, the failures, they become the fixation for you.
sentences.zh: 那些损失、那些失败，成了你执念的焦点。

sentences.en: So there is this theory called the 50-50 principle, which essentially suggests that for every emotion or positive experience we have, there will be an equal experience or emotion
sentences.zh: 所以有一个叫做50-50原则的理论，它基本上表明，我们经历的每一个情绪或积极体验，都会有一个同等程度的体验或情绪

sentences.en: that will be negative.
sentences.zh: 那就是消极的。

sentences.en: So you get a promotion, your car gets towed.
sentences.zh: 所以你升职了，你的车被拖走了。

sentences.en: You get a free coffee, you stub your toe.
sentences.zh: 你得到了一杯免费咖啡，你的脚趾踢到了桌角。

sentences.en: You go on a great first date, you forget about your really expensive electricity bill.
sentences.zh: 你进行了一次棒极了的初次约会，结果把那个贵的要命的电费单给忘到脑后了。

sentences.en: Quickly reflect on your last week for me here.
sentences.zh: 现在请为我快速回顾一下你过去一周的生活。

sentences.en: I feel like that balance is pretty accurate.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这种平衡相当准确。

sentences.en: Sometimes you have months that are more negative.
sentences.zh: 有时候你会经历消极更多的月份。

sentences.en: Sometimes it makes up for it and you have months that are more positive.
sentences.zh: 有时它会弥补回来，你会迎来更多积极的月份。

sentences.en: But it always comes back to the 50-50.
sentences.zh: 但它总是会回归到50对50。

sentences.en: When we are struggling with being happy with what we have, this theory would essentially suggest that it's not because nothing good or amazing is happening,
sentences.zh: 当我们苦于无法对拥有的东西感到满意时，这个理论基本上会表明，这不是因为没有什么好事或惊艳的事发生

sentences.en: but that we're focusing too much on the negative experience that are always going to occur.
sentences.zh: 而是因为我们把太多的注意力放在了那些无论如何都会发生的消极经历上。

sentences.en: Or we forget to appreciate what is good and therefore we start seeing things that are actually positive as a letdown because perhaps our expectations
sentences.zh: 或者我们忘记去欣赏美好的事物，因此我们开始把那些实际上很积极的事情看作是一种让人失望的事，也许是因为我们的期望

sentences.en: for the 50% that is good in our life is just too high.
sentences.zh: 对于生活中那50%的美好事物来说实在太高了。

sentences.en: So returning to what I was saying before, what does this headspace of never being happy with what we have look like?
sentences.zh: 所以回到我刚才的话题，这种永远无法对拥有的东西感到满意的精神状态到底是什么样子的呢？

sentences.en: Well, firstly, often what it's going to manifest as is obsessive future planning and a real difficulty staying present.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，它的表现往往是强迫性的未来规划，并且非常难以活在当下。

sentences.en: This is also known as when, then thinking.
sentences.zh: 这也常被称为“当……时，就会……”思维模式。

sentences.en: So when I get this, then I'll be happy.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我得到这个时，我就会快乐。

sentences.en: When I get the job, when I get the partner, when I get the shiny new object, this has another name.
sentences.zh: 当我得到了工作，得到了伴侣，得到了闪亮的新物件时……这种心态还有另一个名字。

sentences.en: It's called the arrival fallacy.
sentences.zh: 它叫做“抵达谬误”。

sentences.en: When I arrive at this arbitrary point, I will be ecstatic.
sentences.zh: 当我抵达这个随心所欲的节点时，我就会欣喜若狂。

sentences.en: My life will make sense.
sentences.zh: 我的生活就会有意义了。

sentences.en: That point, of course, though, always keeps moving.
sentences.zh: 然而，那个节点当然总是在不断移动。

sentences.en: You know, how many of us are constantly waiting for something and waiting so intently, we kind of forget that the chapter we're in now is just as sweet, it's just as important.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们中有多少人一直在等待着什么，等待得如此专注，以至于我们有点忘记了我们现在所处的这个章节同样美妙，同样重要。

sentences.en: Sometimes you really have to question, like, what is enough for me?
sentences.zh: 有时候你真的不得不发出疑问，比如，究竟什么对我和说是“够了”？

sentences.en: What is this secret, you know, secret doorway that I will one day walk through that will make me finally happy?
sentences.zh: 这个神秘的，你知道的，能让我有一天走过去并最终获得幸福的神秘之门究竟在哪里？

sentences.en: Objectively, when we're experiencing a severe lack of basic needs, getting certain things like job security, more income, stable shelter,
sentences.zh: 客观地说，当我们经历严重的缺乏基本需求时，获得某些东西比如工作保障、更高的收入、稳定的住所

sentences.en: you know, that's certainly going to increase our happiness levels.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那肯定会提高我们的幸福水平。

sentences.en: The happiness jump between having very little to having enough to sustain you and then having enough to be comfortable, those jumps are very, very large.
sentences.zh: 从一无所有到拥有足够维持生活的物资，再到拥有足够舒适的生活，这几次幸福感的跨越是非常非常巨大的。

sentences.en: But once you are comfortable from there, we really don't realize how minor and incremental the change to our happiness level will be.
sentences.zh: 但一旦你从此衣食无忧，我们真的很难意识到，我们幸福感的改变其实是多么的微小和渐进。

sentences.en: But we place so much pressure on what are actually really small changes to transform our lives when we already have, you know, actually so much.
sentences.zh: 然而，当我们实际上已经拥有了非常多的东西时，却把巨大的压力寄托在那些实际上很小的改变上，指望它们来改变我们的生活。

sentences.en: You may also find that, you know, when you do achieve the big things that you previously told yourself would be enough for you, you still feel quite empty.
sentences.zh: 你可能还会发现，当你真正实现了以前告诉自己就足够的大事时，你仍然会感到相当空虚。

sentences.en: I think this is actually the biggest indicator of them all.
sentences.zh: 我认为这实际上是所有迹象中最显著的一个。

sentences.en: You say, you know, when I graduate from university, then my life is going to start and then you walk across the stage.
sentences.zh: 你说，你知道的，等我从大学毕业，我的生活就要开始了，然后你走上了毕业典礼的舞台。

sentences.en: Nothing really changes.
sentences.zh: 其实什么都没有改变。

sentences.en: You finally get into the relationship, but you find that, you know, even the most perfect person isn't going to eliminate all other struggles in your life.
sentences.zh: 你终于谈上了恋爱，却发现，哪怕是最完美的人也无法消除你生活中的所有其他挣扎。

sentences.en: Another indicator that you're not happy with what you have, envy or jealousy towards the people you perceive have it all.
sentences.zh: 另一个标明你对现状不满的迹象，是对你认为拥有一切的人产生羡慕或嫉妒。

sentences.en: And with that, probably also some frustration and self-hatred.
sentences.zh: 伴随而来的，可能还有一些沮丧和自我厌恶。

sentences.en: You know, that heavy feeling in your body, that battle between, you know, feeling envious of someone else and then trying to rein it in and control your ego
sentences.zh: 你知道那种身体里的沉重感，那种一方面对别人感到羡慕，另一方面又试图克制并控制自我意识的挣扎

sentences.en: and then feeling envious and being like, why am I thinking this way?
sentences.zh: 然后感到嫉妒，心里想：我为什么会这样想？

sentences.en: I'm such a bad person, but you can't stop it.
sentences.zh: 我真是个糟糕的人，但你又停不下来。

sentences.en: Then you feel guilty.
sentences.zh: 接着你就会感到内疚。

sentences.en: It's just a constant spiral.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一个无休止的恶性循环。

sentences.en: Persistent restlessness.
sentences.zh: 挥之不去的焦躁不安。

sentences.en: Now this can manifest in a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 这种情况可以表现在很多方面。

sentences.en: There's frequent job or relationship hopping, even constantly moving cities, countries,
sentences.zh: 经常频繁地跳槽、换恋爱对象，甚至不断搬去不同的城市、国家，

sentences.en: anything to find the place, the person, the thing that could finally, you know, change everything for you.
sentences.zh: 只要能找到那个地方、那个人、那件最终能，你知道的，为你改变一切的事物就行。

sentences.en: This is a common thing we see in our 20s, right?
sentences.zh: 这是我们在二十多岁时常见的情况，对吧？

sentences.en: Honestly, I'm guilty of it.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我也曾深陷其中。

sentences.en: I moved to Sydney after a breakup because I thought it would change my life.
sentences.zh: 分手后我搬到了悉尼，因为我以为这会改变我的生活。

sentences.en: And trust me, it did not have that immediate effect.
sentences.zh: 相信我，它并没有带来那种立竿见影的效果。

sentences.en: In fact, it probably made it harder in the first year.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在第一年里它可能让事情变得更艰难了。

sentences.en: The geographic cure.
sentences.zh: 地理位置疗法。

sentences.en: Once I move to this place, I'll be happy.
sentences.zh: 只要我搬到这个地方，我就会幸福。

sentences.en: If I just pick up everything and move cities, my whole life will change and I'll forget about all these issues.
sentences.zh: 如果我收拾好一切搬去别的城市，我的整个人生都会改变，我就会忘掉所有这些烦恼。

sentences.en: The geographic cure is a myth.
sentences.zh: 地理位置疗法纯属无稽之谈。

sentences.en: To offer you some evidence of this, in one study in 2012, the researcher David Kahneman asked a group of individuals living in one part of the US, specifically the Midwest,
sentences.zh: 为了给你提供一些证据，在2012年的一项研究中，研究人员大卫·卡尼曼询问了一群生活在美国某一地区的人，具体来说是中西部，

sentences.en: do you think people living in Southern California are happier?
sentences.zh: 你们觉得住在南加州的人会更幸福吗？

sentences.en: The majority of them were like, yeah, of course they are.
sentences.zh: 他们大多数人的反应都是：废话，当然了。

sentences.en: It's beautiful.
sentences.zh: 那里风景优美。

sentences.en: It's sunny.
sentences.zh: 阳光灿烂。

sentences.en: Who wouldn't be happier there?
sentences.zh: 谁在那里会不开心呢？

sentences.en: He then asked, do you think you'd be happier if you moved there?
sentences.zh: 接着他又问：如果你搬到那里，你觉得自己会更幸福吗？

sentences.en: A majority of them said, yes, they would.
sentences.zh: 大多数人都回答会是的。

sentences.en: But when he actually compared life satisfaction scores between the two cities, he found that they were nearly identical.
sentences.zh: 但当他实际对比了这两个地方人们的生活满意度评分时，他发现它们几乎一模一样。

sentences.en: So all these individuals in the Midwest, and you could replace the Midwest with really any country, any city, there's always going to be this beautiful, romanticized city
sentences.zh: 所以，中西部这些地方的所有人——其实你可以把中西部替换成任何国家、任何城市，总会有这样一个美丽且被浪漫化的城市

sentences.en: that we think when we move to it will change our lives and everyone there is happy and thriving.
sentences.zh: 让我们觉得只要搬过去生活就会改变，那里的每个人都幸福且蒸蒸日上。

sentences.en: But what he found was that actually, it doesn't really change much.
sentences.zh: 但他的发现是，其实它并不会带来多大改变。

sentences.en: It's nearly identical.
sentences.zh: 几乎一模一样。

sentences.en: Location isn't the thing that is going to change your life.
sentences.zh: 改变你生活的并不是地理位置。

sentences.en: It's the perception of your life or the perception of the place that does that.
sentences.zh: 对生活的看法，或者对那个地方的看法，才能做到这一点。

sentences.en: Another study from 2016, this time in the UK, found something very similar, but it also found that moving cities actually makes you more stressed, more detached, more lonely.
sentences.zh: 2016年的另一项研究，这次是在英国进行的，得出了非常相似的结论，但它还发现，搬家实际上会让你感到更压力山大、更加疏离、更加孤独。

sentences.en: So a warning to anyone in their 20s right now,
sentences.zh: 所以，给现在所有二十多岁的人一个警告，

sentences.en: I'm talking to you, if you think a sudden move is going to finally make you happier, the story is a lot more complex.
sentences.zh: 我就是在对你说的，如果你以为一次突然的搬家最终能让你更幸福，那这个故事要复杂得多。

sentences.en: A few other signs here that you're struggling to find happiness with what you have, no matter how much you receive or achieve, you catastrophize small setbacks,
sentences.zh: 这里还有其他一些迹象表明，你很难对现有的东西感到满意，无论你得到或取得了多少成就，你都会把小挫折灾难化，

sentences.en: you can be quite impulsive, especially with money, you over consume lifestyle content that is idealistic and romanticized, you may spend more time online shopping
sentences.zh: 你可能会相当冲动，尤其是在金钱方面，你过度消费那些理想化和被浪漫化的生活方式内容，你可能会花更多时间在网上购物

sentences.en: or scrolling dating apps and your mood is seemingly linked to your external accomplishments and what you have rather than your internal sense of satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 或者刷约会软件，而且你的情绪似乎与你的外在成就以及你拥有的东西息息相关，而不是源于你内在的满足感。

sentences.en: So if this sounds like you, I want to explain why this may be happening because it can be seriously confronting, especially when we start to perhaps realize, wait, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果这听起来很像你，我想解释一下为什么会这样，因为这可能会非常直面且扎心，特别是当我们开始意识到：等等，你知道的，

sentences.en: what would I need to finally be content?
sentences.zh: 我到底需要什么才能最终感到满足？

sentences.en: And if I don't get that, will I ever be happy?
sentences.zh: 如果我得不到那个，我还能幸福吗？

sentences.en: Is there a final destination, a final spot I wish to be?
sentences.zh: 真的存在一个最终的目的地、一个我渴望抵达的最终地点吗？

sentences.en: Does that even exist?
sentences.zh: 那东西真的存在吗？

sentences.en: So essentially, when we have this more, more, more mindset, when we can't be happy with what we have, what is occurring is something called hedonic adaptation.
sentences.zh: 所以从本质上讲，当我们抱着这种“多多益善”的心态，当我们对拥有的东西感到不满足时，发生的事情被称为享乐适应。

sentences.en: It's also called the hedonism treadmill.
sentences.zh: 它也被称为享乐跑步机。

sentences.en: So this was first given a name in the 1970s by two Canadian researchers,
sentences.zh: 这个概念最早是在20世纪70年代由两位加拿大研究人员提出的，

sentences.en: Brickman and Campbell.
sentences.zh: 布里克曼和坎贝尔。

sentences.en: And what they found is that humans, no matter what's happening in their life, you know, they could win a Guarami, they could marry the love of their life, they could also
sentences.zh: 他们发现，人类无论生活中发生什么，你知道的，他们可能赢得格莱美奖，可能和一生挚爱结婚，也可能会

sentences.en: lose the love of their life, could lose everything.
sentences.zh: 失去一生的挚爱，甚至失去一切。

sentences.en: We will still typically return to a fairly stable baseline level of happiness that seems to be largely
sentences.zh: 我们通常仍然会回归到一个相当稳定的基准幸福水平，这个水平似乎在很大程度上是

sentences.en: predetermined, regardless of what is happening around us.
sentences.zh: 预先决定好的，无论我们周围正发生着什么。

sentences.en: Now, this is specifically the case, or especially the case, I should say, with really happy, positive events.
sentences.zh: 现在，这种情况尤其——或者说特别会体现在那些非常快乐、积极的事件上。

sentences.en: You know, you land your dream job, but that, the ecstasy of that doesn't last that long.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你找到了梦想的工作，但那种狂喜并不会持续太久。

sentences.en: You know, it's not long until you start to notice the downsides, or you get into a relationship, and it's amazing and thrilling until the novelty wears off, and then you kind of
sentences.zh: 没过多久你就会开始注意到它的缺点，或者你陷入了一段恋情，它美妙而令人兴奋，直到新鲜感消退，然后你就会

sentences.en: return back to that stable level.
sentences.zh: 回归到那个稳定的水平。

sentences.en: This is basically our brain's way of maintaining emotional balance, but it also means that we rarely feel happy and satisfied for long.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是我们大脑维持情绪平衡的方式，但也意味着我们很少能长时间感到幸福和满足。

sentences.en: The big things we think will change our life, they actually don't end up changing that much in the long term, but because we expect that they will, we also equally feel
sentences.zh: 那些我们以为会改变生活的重大事情，从长远来看其实最终并没有改变多少，但因为我们期望它们能改变，所以我们感到的

sentences.en: even more let down.
sentences.zh: 失落感也同样更加强烈。

sentences.en: The psychologist
sentences.zh: 心理学家

sentences.en: Sonia Lubomirsky, she wrote the book
sentences.zh: 索尼娅·柳博米尔斯基，她写了一本名为

sentences.en: The Myth of Happiness, she added on to this research, and she discovered that only around
sentences.zh: 《幸福的迷思》的书，她在这些研究的基础上继续深入，并发现大约只有

sentences.en: 10% of our happiness comes from external circumstances.
sentences.zh: 10%的幸福感来自外部环境。

sentences.en: Only 10%, around 40% comes from attitude and your intentional mindset,
sentences.zh: 只有10%，大约40%来自态度和你的刻意心态，

sentences.en: 50% is actually genetically determined.
sentences.zh: 而50%其实是由基因决定的。

sentences.en: Yet that, that 10%, that is where we put most of our focus on.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们却把大部分的关注点都放在了那10%上面。

sentences.en: We think, if I just had this one more thing,
sentences.zh: 我们总觉得，如果我能再得到这件东西，

sentences.en: I'd finally feel whole, if I just achieved this,
sentences.zh: 我就终于能感到完整了；如果我能取得这个成就，

sentences.en: I'd finally be happy.
sentences.zh: 我最终就会幸福。

sentences.en: Once we get to it, we recalibrate, the happiness we expected doesn't laSt.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们得到了，我们就会重新校准，我们所期望的幸福并不能持久。

sentences.en: That's hedonic adaptation at work.
sentences.zh: 这就是享乐适应在起作用。

sentences.en: We're always resetting the bar.
sentences.zh: 我们总是在不断重置标准。

sentences.en: Basically, what I'm trying to say through this is it's not you, it's your human blueprint trying to kind of almost humble us, it seeMs.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我想通过这一点表达的是，这不是你的问题，而是你的基因蓝图似乎在试图让我们保持谦逊。

sentences.en: Our brain chemistry also plays a major role.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑化学物质也扮演着重要角色。

sentences.en: Of course, if we're going to talk about happiness at some stage, we're going to talk about dopamine.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果我们要在某个阶段谈论幸福，我们就不得不谈谈多巴胺。

sentences.en: Dopamine, it's not just the happiness chemical, it's the neurotransmitter associated with motivation, reward, and pleasure.
sentences.zh: 多巴胺不仅是“快乐化学物质”，它还是与动机、奖励和愉悦感相关的神经递质。

sentences.en: But here's the thing that most of us don't know about dopamine, and I don't think I even ended up learning about this until I was in my third year of studying psychology.
sentences.zh: 但大多数人不知道的是，关于多巴胺这一点，我觉得自己直到学心理学的第三年才最终了解到这一点。

sentences.en: Your dopamine doesn't spike when you get the reward, but in anticipation of it.
sentences.zh: 你的多巴胺并不是在获得奖励时飙升，而是在期待奖励的时候。

sentences.en: I was always told, you know, when you eat a chocolate bar, it makes you happy.
sentences.zh: 我过去总是被告知，你知道的，当你吃一块巧克力时，它会让你快乐。

sentences.en: When you do this, it makes you happy.
sentences.zh: 当你做这个时，它会让你快乐。

sentences.en: It's the anticipation of it that makes you feel happy and the relief of finally getting it.
sentences.zh: 其实是对它的期待让你感到快乐，以及最终得到它时的解脱感。

sentences.en: So when you're fantasizing about the next big thing, your brain floods with dopamine, you feel excited, you feel hopeful, you feel alive.
sentences.zh: 所以当你幻想着下一个重大目标时，你的大脑就会涌入多巴胺，你会感到兴奋，感到充满希望，感到充满生机。

sentences.en: You know, think about the excitement before a first date or a big overseas trip, but once you actually get it, the dopamine drop-off from that leaves you feeling flat,
sentences.zh: 你想想看，在第一次约会或一次重大的海外旅行之前的那种兴奋感，但一旦你真正得到了它，多巴胺的骤降会让你感到索然无味，

sentences.en: even disappointed.
sentences.zh: 甚至感到失望。

sentences.en: It's why people, you know, they go to their dream destinations, they go to Paris, they go to Thailand, they go to Rome, and they're like,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么人们，你知道的，他们去他们的梦想目的地，他们去巴黎，他们去泰国，他们去罗马，然后他们却觉得：

sentences.en: I'm kind of disappointed.
sentences.zh: 我有点失望。

sentences.en: It's not what my expectations were.
sentences.zh: 这和我的期望不一样。

sentences.en: Or their wedding day or a big milestone, you know, maybe they don't end up leaving that feeling as happy as they thought they would.
sentences.zh: 或者他们的婚礼日或某个重大里程碑，你知道的，也许他们最终离开时并没有想象中那么快乐。

sentences.en: But this explains why we feel addicted to the act of setting very huge goals, but not necessarily fulfilled when we get the thing.
sentences.zh: 但这解释了为什么我们会对设定宏伟目标的行为上瘾，但在达成目标时却未必能感到充实。

sentences.en: We're not actually addicted to achievement, we're addicted to the feeling of almoSt.
sentences.zh: 我们其实不是对成就上瘾，我们是对“差一点就得到”的感觉上瘾。

sentences.en: This can lead to something I call a success hangover.
sentences.zh: 这可能会导致我所说的“成功宿醉”。

sentences.en: It's also known as gold medal syndrome for a more formal name you'd find in a psychology textbook.
sentences.zh: 在心理学教科书里，它还有一个更正式的名字叫“金牌综合征”。

sentences.en: Gold medal syndrome, of course, named after Olympians who work their entire freaking lives for one moment for a gold medal and then they get it and they're like, oh,
sentences.zh: 金牌综合征，当然是因那些为了赢得一枚金牌而拼尽全副精力的奥运健儿而得名，当他们终于拿到金牌时，他们的反应却是：啊，

sentences.en: this is it?
sentences.zh: 这就完了？

sentences.en: This is all I ever wanted?
sentences.zh: 这就是我一直想要的全部吗？

sentences.en: Now what?
sentences.zh: 接下来该怎么办？

sentences.en: What do I do after this?
